plan.title: Paired 3-condition DE: control vs treatment A vs treatment B (blood)
plan.analytical_narrative: Four subjects each contribute a control, treated_a, and treated_b blood sample (12000 x 13 raw Salmon gene counts). This is a within-subject repeated-measures design with three levels of one factor, so the subject is modeled as a blocking term to remove between-subject variance before testing the condition effect. Step 1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm subjects pair up as expected and no sample is an outlier before any test is fit. Step 2 fits DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition on a minimally pre-filtered count matrix (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest group size), using median-of-ratios normalization internal to DESeq2. An LRT (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) answers 'which genes respond to either treatment' as one omnibus test per gene; three pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b, control as the explicit reference level) answer the direction and 'do the two treatments differ from each other'. Each contrast gets ashr shrinkage (contrasts between non-reference levels require ashr, not apeglm) and BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, applied within each contrast separately. Step 3 runs fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic for each of the three contrasts against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) then Reactome and WikiPathways human (follow-up), all present in the reference store, respecting the 15-500 gene set size window. Step 4 assembles the report: fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the gene tables with both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC, per-contrast DE gene counts and overlap/summary across contrasts, leading-edge genes for significant pathways, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene set collection versions).
